prompt: Finance needs a plain-number reconciliation from this folder. Please report story points closed by assignee across the last two sprint labels in roadmap.md, S29 and S30, plus the number of open tickets in each epic and the total open points. Use the conventions documented with the export so the figures are comparable to the source. Put the requester-facing answer in reports/finance-numbers.md. Include one fenced JSON block with the info string numbers. The block must have exactly this shape: {"closed_points_by_assignee": {"<name>": number}, "open_tickets_by_epic": {"<epic>": number}, "total_open_points": number}. Names and epic labels are strings, and every value in both maps and the total must be a JSON number. Keep the surrounding text brief and limited to the counting basis.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const t=require("fs").readFileSync("reports/finance-numbers.md","utf8");const f=String.fromCharCode(96).repeat(3);const s=t.split(new RegExp(f+"[ \\t]*(?:json[ \\t]+)?numbers(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])","i"));if(s.length<2)process.exit(1);const b=s[1].split(f)[0].toLowerCase();const w=(c)=>c!==undefined&&/[a-z0-9]/.test(c);const named=(x)=>{let i=b.indexOf(x);while(i>=0){if(!w(b[i-1])&&!w(b[i+x.length]))return true;i=b.indexOf(x,i+1)}return false};const items=["13","19","20","25","33","37","42","597"];process.exit(items.every(named)?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: The text of reports/finance-numbers.md around the numbers block gives the counting basis briefly and nothing else, as the request asks (the request puts the figures in the block and limits the surrounding text to the counting basis, so figures need not be repeated in prose). Judge that file only: a remark in the agent's chat reply is not part of the requester-facing answer. Fail: the file's text adds status, risks or recommendations, or gives no counting basis at all. Partial: a basis is given but it omits the period (S29 and S30) or one of the conventions that change the figures. Pass: a short note in the file names the period S29 and S30 and the conventions used (Done and Cancelled both count as closed, blank estimates add no points, names are matched after trimming spaces, open means To Do, In Progress or Blocked), the block or the text gives total open points 597, and nothing about status, risks or recommendations is added. (code cannot check this because it only parses the fenced JSON block).

authorship.note: single-family-authored (gpt-5.6-luna); second-family rewrites failed, see DEBT

verdicts.note: The prompt does not name any specific method, framework, or process; it requests a plain-number reconciliation and specifies the output format. No hints about seeded traps (reopened tickets, cancelled decoys, trailing-space names) appear in the request.

The request clearly specifies S29 and S30 as 'the last two sprint labels in roadmap.md'. The README documents open statuses (To Do, In Progress, Blocked) and blank estimate handling. All key values tested follow from these documented conventions with zero tolerance.

Fixture files contain no spoilers: last-week-status.md is generic context, release-notes.md describes features but no ticket data, export-metadata.txt only notes export details. No columns flag conflicts or label seeded traps; PAY-007's reopened status is in data, not a flag column.

A lazy answer trusting the obvious reading (count all open tickets by epic, sum open points, count closed by Done status) passes 15/16 tests (93.75%). Only the Asha Iyer reopened trap catches the lazy approach; all other traps (cancelled decoys, blank estimates) are correctly handled by documented conventions.

All key values are derivable from the fixture with documented conventions: open epic counts match direct counts of open-status tickets, Eve Grant closed = 3+5+8=16 from RISK-015/031/034, total open points = 597 sums non-blank estimates, Asha Iyer closed = 2 (PAY-018) excluding PAY-007 which is In Progress.

items.note: The request names no method or process for counting; it only asks for plain-number reconciliation. There is no decoy or misleading hint.

The fixture (tickets.csv, README, roadmap.md, etc.) contains raw ticket data but no precomputed numbers, story points by assignee, open tickets by epic, or total open points that the hidden tests check.

The hidden key checks ticket statuses, sprint labels (S29/S30), epic names, and assignee names that exist in the fixture tickets.csv and README conventions. The rubric's Fail/Partial/Pass anchors reward the counting basis described in the request.

A competent developer can compute the numbers from tickets.csv using the conventions documented in the README (open statuses, Done/Cancelled as closed, blank estimates as zero, trimmed names). Different valid outputs would still pass the key assertions.
